title: Obtenir une information et rebondir sur la réponse
summary: Ask useful questions, respond to new constraints and clarify details instead of reciting a fixed interview script.
objectives: Choose a question that fills a real gap in the current exchange.
Build a follow-up from the answer just received.
Confirm a date, restriction or inclusion without misrepresenting it.

sources.label: FEI TCF Canada: oral task 2 information-seeking interaction, consulted 2026-09-07
FEI evaluation: interaction, fluency and situation-appropriate language, consulted 2026-09-07

sections.title: Ask for information you actually need
paragraphs: An information-seeking exchange is a joint activity, not a list of unrelated questions. Start with your purpose and the missing detail, then let the answer change your next move. A yes/no question checks a proposition; a question with `quel`, `comment` or `à quelle heure` requests a particular detail.

`Est-ce que` questions and subject–verb questions with rising intonation are ordinary spoken forms. Inversion can also be appropriate, especially in a polite request. Avoid treating the most formal form as the only correct spoken French. Keep `vous` when the fictional relationship is an unfamiliar organiser.
points: A follow-up should not ask for a detail that was already given unless you are deliberately confirming it.
`Une séance` (f.) is a session; `le matériel` (m.) is equipment.

examples.french:
— Bonjour, je voudrais participer à votre atelier photo. **Quel matériel faut-il apporter** ?
— Un téléphone suffit, mais il doit être chargé.
— D'accord. **Et si la batterie se vide**, est-ce qu'on peut la recharger sur place ?
— Oui, dans la salle d'accueil, pas pendant la sortie.
— Donc, il vaut mieux arriver avec une batterie pleine. **Combien de temps dure la sortie** ?
examples.english:
— Hello, I would like to take part in your photography workshop. What equipment do we need to bring?
— A phone is enough, but it must be charged.
— All right. And if the battery runs down, can we recharge it there?
— Yes, in the reception room, not during the outing.
— So it is better to arrive with a full battery. How long does the outing last?
examples.note: Each new question grows out of the previous answer. This is a written demonstration, not listening evidence.

examples.french: **Est-ce que** le parcours convient aux débutants ?
examples.english: Is the route suitable for beginners?
examples.note: A neutral spoken yes/no question checks suitability.

examples.french: Vous proposez aussi une séance en soirée ?
examples.english: Do you also offer an evening session?
examples.note: Subject–verb order with question intonation is normal speech, not defective grammar.

mistakes.avoid: Est-ce que peut-on emprunter un appareil ?
mistakes.prefer: Est-ce qu'on peut emprunter un appareil ?
mistakes.why: Do not combine `est-ce que` with subject-pronoun inversion. `Peut-on emprunter un appareil ?` is also correct without `est-ce que`.

sections.title: Follow the answer, especially when it changes the plan
paragraphs: A useful follow-up can narrow a vague answer, ask about an alternative, or explore a condition. `Dans ce cas` explicitly links your response to new information. If a session is full, asking about another date is more responsive than restarting with a question about its location.

`En` and `y` can avoid unnecessary repetition when their references are clear: `Il reste des places ? Il en reste combien ?` `Y` covers a place or an `à` complement referring to a thing: `Peut-on y participer à distance ?` If several possible references compete, name the session or service instead.
points: Do not turn an unsuccessful request into a demand for an entitlement the scenario never established.
The best next question depends on your purpose; more than one can be sensible in real conversation.

examples.french:
— La séance de samedi est complète.
— **Dans ce cas**, quelle autre date pourriez-vous me proposer ?
examples.english:
— Saturday's session is full.
— In that case, what other date could you offer me?
examples.note: The speaker adapts instead of continuing a memorised Saturday script.

examples.french:
— Il reste quelques places dimanche.
— Il **en** reste assez pour deux personnes ?
examples.english:
— There are a few places left on Sunday.
— Are there enough left for two people?
examples.note: `En` refers back to `places`; the quantity question now serves a concrete need.

examples.french:
— L'activité se déroule dehors, sauf en cas de forte pluie.
— Et dans ce cas, **est-elle reportée ou organisée à l'intérieur** ?
examples.english:
— The activity takes place outdoors, except in heavy rain.
— And in that case, is it postponed or held indoors?
examples.note: The follow-up asks about the stated exception, not a new unrelated topic.

mistakes.avoid: Vous avez des places ? Combien vous restez ?
mistakes.prefer: Vous avez des places ? Combien vous en reste-t-il ?
mistakes.why: In `il vous reste des places`, `il` is the impersonal subject, `vous` is the person for whom places remain, and `en` represents `places`. `Vous restez` asks about you staying, not remaining places.

sections.title: Check the precise boundary before closing
paragraphs: Reformulate with `si j'ai bien compris`, then check the detail that matters. `Avant mardi`, `jusqu'à mardi` and `à partir de mardi` set different boundaries. `Inclus` means included; `en supplément` means extra. If a boundary remains vague, ask explicitly whether the day or item counts.

For FEI oral task 2, the total is 5 minutes 30 seconds, including 2 minutes of preparation, leaving about 3 minutes 30 seconds of interaction. Use preparation to identify information gaps and possible branches, not to write and read a complete speech. The short model below illustrates moves; it is not a full-length timed performance.
points: Clarification is evidence of active interaction, not automatically a failure.
A written dialogue cannot establish comprehension of a live response, turn-taking speed, intelligibility or spontaneous fluency.

examples.french: Quand vous dites « jusqu'à mardi », **mardi est-il compris** ?
examples.english: When you say "until Tuesday," does that include Tuesday?
examples.note: The question resolves a boundary instead of silently assuming it.

examples.french: Si j'ai bien compris, le prêt est inclus, **mais pas** l'impression des photos. C'est bien cela ?
examples.english: If I have understood correctly, the loan is included, but printing the photos is not. Is that right?
examples.note: The contrast carries the exact inclusion/exclusion distinction into the check.

practice.prompt: After Un téléphone suffit, mais il doit être chargé, which follow-up addresses the new constraint?
choices: Peut-on recharger le téléphone sur place ?
Faut-il vraiment un téléphone, puisque vous venez de le dire ?
answers: Peut-on recharger le téléphone sur place ?
practice.explanation: The charging requirement motivates a practical follow-up.

practice.prompt: Keep est-ce que and remove only the inversion: Est-ce que peut-on venir sans appareil ? Write the corrected whole question.
answers: Est-ce qu'on peut venir sans appareil ?
practice.explanation: After est-ce que, use on peut; que contracts to qu' before on.

practice.prompt: Supply the pronoun replacing places: Des places dimanche ? Il ___ reste combien ?
practice.explanation: En refers to the previously mentioned places and combines with a quantity.

practice.prompt: The organiser says Inscrivez-vous jusqu'à mardi. You need to know whether Tuesday itself is allowed. Choose the precise clarification.
practice.explanation: The question checks the deadline boundary rather than an unrelated detail.

practice.prompt: Supply the three-word expression beginning with à for asking the start time: ___ commence la visite ? Use the appropriate form of quel with heure.
practice.explanation: À quelle heure asks at what time; quelle agrees with the feminine noun heure.

practice.prompt: Use the exact three-word linking expression taught: La séance est annulée. ___, peut-on choisir une autre date ?
practice.explanation: Dans ce cas makes the alternative request depend on the cancellation.

practice.prompt: You need two places together. The organiser says Il reste une place vendredi et plusieurs dimanche. Which follow-up best serves that need?
choices: Pourquoi n'y a-t-il qu'une place vendredi ?
practice.explanation: Sunday is the offered option with enough capacity for two; the question uses the answer just given.

practice.prompt: Read: Le casque est fourni, mais les gants ne le sont pas. Copy only the two-word noun phrase naming what you must bring if needed.
practice.explanation: The helmet is provided; the gloves are excluded.

practice.prompt: Form only the inversion of vous pouvez, preserving pouvoir in the present.
practice.explanation: Simple inversion joins the verb and subject pronoun with a hyphen.

practice.prompt: Read: Les réservations commencent à partir de jeudi. Is a reservation on Wednesday supported?
choices: Non, l'ouverture des réservations est jeudi.
answers: Non, l'ouverture des réservations est jeudi.
practice.explanation: À partir de marks the start; it is not a deadline before which to act.

practice.prompt: Use the place pronoun: L'inscription se fait au comptoir. Peut-on ___ payer aussi ?
practice.explanation: Y replaces au comptoir, the place where payment might also be possible.

practice.prompt: Supply only comprendre in the past participle: Si j'ai bien ___, le repas n'est pas inclus.
practice.explanation: Si j'ai bien compris introduces a check of what was understood, not an assertion of certainty.

practice.prompt: Supply only the direct-question word asking how, not when: ___ peut-on modifier une réservation ?
practice.explanation: Comment asks for the procedure, rather than its time.

practice.prompt: The guide says Les enfants sont acceptés à partir de huit ans. You are coming with a seven-year-old. Which reply correctly handles the restriction?
choices: Existe-t-il une activité adaptée aux enfants de sept ans ?
Je vais réserver ici pour sept ans sans vous le dire.
answers: Existe-t-il une activité adaptée aux enfants de sept ans ?
practice.explanation: The speaker respects the stated threshold and asks for an alternative.

practice.prompt: Copy only the two words that mean an extra charge rather than inclusion: La visite est comprise ; le repas est en supplément.
practice.explanation: The meal is extra, even though the visit is included.

practice.prompt: Read: Nous pouvons vous prêter un appareil, mais seulement sur réservation. Copy the three-word restriction starting with seulement, without a final full stop.
practice.explanation: The offer is conditional on reservation; a useful follow-up would ask how to reserve.

production_task.prompt: Original spoken task: You want to join a community cooking workshop with a friend. Spend two minutes listing information gaps, then interact with a partner for about three and a half minutes. Ask about availability, equipment and a practical constraint. The partner should introduce an unexpected change, such as a full session or different venue. Follow up, clarify one detail and confirm the next step. Without a partner, record your questions and possible branches, but label this solo rehearsal, not live interaction. The model is a short illustration, not a full timed answer. Self-review only.
production_task.model_answer:
— Bonjour, je cherche un atelier de cuisine pour deux personnes. Est-ce qu'il reste des places samedi ?
— Il n'en reste qu'une, mais nous avons une séance dimanche.
— Dans ce cas, pourriez-vous nous inscrire dimanche ? À quelle heure faut-il arriver ?
— À neuf heures quarante-cinq. Attention, la séance aura lieu dans notre autre cuisine.
— Merci de me le préciser. Pourriez-vous me donner l'adresse exacte ? Et faut-il apporter du matériel ?
— Je vous enverrai l'adresse. Apportez seulement un tablier et une boîte pour emporter votre préparation.
— Une boîte par personne, c'est bien cela ?
— Oui.
— Très bien. Donc, nous serons deux dimanche à neuf heures quarante-cinq, avec un tablier et une boîte chacun. Comment dois-je confirmer la réservation ?
production_task.translation:
— Hello, I am looking for a cooking workshop for two people. Are there any places left on Saturday?
— There is only one left, but we have a session on Sunday.
— In that case, could you register us for Sunday? What time should we arrive?
— At nine forty-five. Please note that the session will take place in our other kitchen.
— Thank you for pointing that out. Could you give me the exact address? And do we need to bring any equipment?
— I will send you the address. Just bring an apron and a container to take home what you have made.
— One container per person, is that right?
— Yes.
— Very good. So there will be two of us on Sunday at nine forty-five, with an apron and a container each. How should I confirm the booking?
rubric: I obtain information that serves my purpose, rather than merely asking many memorised questions.
At least one follow-up depends on the partner's actual answer; I handle the unexpected change.
I confirm an important boundary, inclusion, time or quantity without introducing an incorrect fact.
I review intelligibility, turn-taking and question formation. A transcript or solo rehearsal cannot independently establish live interaction or listening readiness.
